description: Bismuth is a chemical element with symbol Bi and atomic number 83. It is a post-transition metal and one of the pnictogens, with chemical properties resembling arsenic and antimony. Elemental bismuth occurs naturally, and its sulfide and oxide forms are important commercial ores.
uses: Bismuth compounds are used in cosmetics, pigments, and pharmaceuticals such as bismuth subsalicylate for treating diarrhea. Its unusual expansion upon solidification made it useful in casting printing type, and suitable bismuth alloys have gained popularity as replacements for lead in various applications.
characteristics: Bismuth is a brittle metal with a silvery-white color that develops a rosy cast from surface oxidation and can display iridescent colors from thin-film interference. It is the most diamagnetic element, has among the highest electrical resistivity and lowest thermal conductivity of all metals, and expands 3.32% upon solidification. It has unusually low toxicity for a heavy metal and was long regarded as the heaviest stable nuclide before being found slightly radioactive in 2003.
